key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved solar conversion with graphene-enabled environmental protection.
engineering_relevance: Combining optical, electrical, and barrier functions offers a route to more efficient and durable planar hybrid silicon photovoltaics.
method: Fabricate planar PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon.
Benchmark against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Evaluate optoelectronic performance and efficiency retention during 75 days of ambient exposure.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% efficiency versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75-day ambient aging; longer-term durability and scalable fabrication of defect-free graphene barriers remain unestablished.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
